schemas.title: ActivityFeedData
schemas.description: Data of an activity_feed widget: the items of the feed, in the delivered order the list keeps.

items.description: 0 to 200 items in the delivered order, which the feed keeps and shows, its Show more button revealing them by page. An empty list is the empty state. Each item needs a time and a title, and may carry a text, a tone of the shared tones, and a link target, which the shared link rule judges. A time no date reads as is legal here: the widget's own cross-check fails the cell naming the item by its position.

time.description: When the item happened: an ISO 8601 date-time, its zone as Z or an offset written +hh:mm, +hhmm or +hh (each with its minus form), a date-time without a zone reading in the viewer's zone, or a bare YYYY-MM-DD date (its UTC midnight, the one date rule of the widgets). The widget cross-checks that a date reads as one, and a time that does not fails the cell naming the item's position.

title.description: The one line of the item, beside its time: the link text when the item carries a target.

text.description: An optional line under the title, which wraps.

tone.description: The shared tone of the item's mark beside its title, written in text for assistive technology; a neutral item draws no mark. Without it, no mark.

href.description: The link target of the title, judged by the shared link rule: a refused one shows the title as text, and the cell does not fail.

schemas.title: ActivityFeedRender
schemas.description: Render of an activity_feed widget: its presentation fields, closed.

time_style.description: How an item writes its time: relative from the host clock, in the host language's relative wording (such as "3 days ago"), or absolute as the host language writes the date and, for a date-time, its time of day. Without it, relative.

page_size.description: How many items the feed shows before its Show more button, which reveals the next page_size items in the delivered order, and disappears when everything is shown. Without it, 10.

show_tone.description: Whether an item of a tone carries its mark beside the title, named in text for assistive technology. Without it, true.
